answer: Make each identity prove continuity. Every few epochs the network quietly asks an agent to extend a private note it committed to earlier, say a sketch of a juniper growing on the tundra, and to add one detail, like the umber of its bark, that matches a hash it posted then. A real agent keeps its own working memory and answers in seconds. An operator running a thousand shells must store and serve a separate history for each, and any identity that fumbles its own past forfeits its stake and its pending rewards.
